Virginia Leaders Reach Marijuana Compromise; Retail Sales Targeted for July 2027  By Charles Womack Star-Tribune Staff Report  RICHMOND, Va. — Virginia lawmakers and Gov. Abigail Spanberger announced Tuesday they have reached a compromise that could bring legal recreational marijuana sales to the commonwealth beginning July 1, 2027.  The agreement follows Spanberger's May 19 veto of legislation that would have established a retail cannabis market. State leaders said the new proposal is designed to address concerns raised during the legislative process while giving regulators additional time to develop rules for the industry.  Virginia legalized possession of up to one ounce of marijuana for adults 21 and older on July 1, 2021. Since then, adults have been allowed to possess limited amounts of marijuana, but the state has not created a legal system for recreational retail sales.  Under the agreement announced Tuesday, state officials would spend the next year developing regulations governing licensing, testing, enforcement and retail operations. Supporters say a regulated marketplace would provide consumer protections and help move cannabis sales into a legal, monitored system.  The proposal is expected to be considered as part of ongoing state budget negotiations. Lawmakers must still approve the plan before it can become law.  For residents of Danville and Pittsylvania County, the announcement does not immediately change current law. Recreational marijuana sales remain illegal in Virginia outside the state's medical cannabis program.  If approved, licensed recreational marijuana sales would begin statewide on July 1, 2027. | Cannabis
